subject: Regional surge tolerance & latency waiver — proposed order form exhibit
messages:
From: Elena Martinez <elena@cardiotech.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@cardiotech.com, Legal - CardioTech <legal@cardiotech.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Latency waiver and surge tolerance language for order form exhibit

Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement had two gating asks before we can finalize the order form: a regional latency tolerance clause for our EU traffic and an explicit surge-tolerance carveout for seasonal peaks (we run occasional batch re-processing and can tolerate slightly higher tail latency for short windows). Legal wants the exhibit language to specify measurable thresholds, duration caps, and an operations evidence path for credits.

Key asks: 
- A short waiver that allows up to 5% of requests to exceed the 99th percentile latency for a contiguous 30-minute window during declared "batch maintenance" events (we'll declare windows in advance when possible).
- A cap on service credits tied to those events (CardioTech requests credits not to exceed single-month invoice x1.25).
- An evidence path: Redwood must provide a post-event latency report, KV cache/trace snapshots, and an ops runbook entry.

Attached: our suggested OrderForm_v3 with placeholder exhibit text and a brief ops checklist. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept this as an addendum to the MSA / SOW, and what evidence we should reasonably expect to provide?

Appreciate the help — procurement is on a tight timeline.

Best,
Elena Martinez
Senior Procurement Manager
CardioTech Inc.
[Attachment: CardioTech_OrderForm_v3.pdf]

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: Elena Martinez <elena@cardiotech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Latency waiver and surge tolerance language for order form exhibit

Elena —

Thanks for the clear asks and the draft. We can support a controlled surge-tolerance carveout, but I want to align internal ops and legal on the exact thresholds and the evidence we commit to. High-level responses: 

- Waiver window: Redwood is open to a limited "maintenance/batch" exception. We prefer advance declaration where possible; for emergency/retroactive declarations we will require post-event notification within 48 hours.
- Threshold: 5% above 99th pctl for a contiguous 30-minute window is plausible, but ops recommends tying the metric to p99 for the specific route/model and aggregating by region (e.g., eu-west-1).
- Credits: we can cap credits, but our standard protection is to limit credits to a single billing period invoice *not to exceed 1.0x. We can consider 1.25x as a special-case uplift subject to SOC-2 operational evidence.
- Evidence: ops can provide latency histograms, request IDs sample (redacted), and our KV-cache hit-rate snapshot. We'll attach an ops runbook excerpt showing how we compute the metrics.

I'll loop in Marissa (contracts) and Ben (SRE evidence owner) for proposed order-form exhibit language and to confirm the documentation we'll attach to the SOW. Can you confirm whether CardioTech requires the surge events to be pre-approved to qualify for the higher credit cap? That will affect our acceptance flow.

Next steps: 
1) I'll send a drafted exhibit with two options (pre-declared events vs. retroactive emergency events) and the evidence checklist.
2) Ben will upload limited sample evidence formats.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: ops-surge-runbook-v1.md]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:23:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Latency waiver and surge tolerance language for order form exhibit

Jordan / Ben —

Looping you both for contract and evidence guidance. Jordan, please find below my redline suggestions for the exhibit. Ben, please confirm whether the listed evidence types are exportable from our telemetry tooling and include approximate turnaround times.

My suggested redlines (high level):
- Replace ad-hoc percentage language with region-specific p99 uplift allowance and a maximum contiguous duration of 30 minutes.
- Define "declared event" vs "emergency event" and require CardioTech to include event window and scope in the ticket portal for pre-declared cases.
- For emergency events, allow a retroactive claim window of 5 business days and require Redwood to provide fully redacted telemetry within 7 business days.
- Service credit cap: propose Redwood standard (1.0x) as baseline; capacity to grant a one-time uplift to 1.25x only with SOC-2 operational evidence submission and executive approval.

Please find my redline doc in the shared drive link and let me know if the language looks acceptable to present to CardioTech legal.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Contracts Counsel | Redwood Inference
[Link: https://redwood-drive.example.com/link/ops-runbook]

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Latency waiver and surge tolerance language for order form exhibit

Quick ops check —

We can produce the following artifacts within the timelines Marissa requests: 
- Latency histogram exports for the affected route (CSV) — available within 48 hours after request.
- Sample request IDs + redacted traces (for a 30-minute window) — available within 72 hours, subject to privacy scrubbing.
- KV-cache hit-rate snapshots and model-specific perf summary — available in 48 hours.

Notes and constraints: 
1) We need CardioTech to identify the model/route by name (or provide sample request IDs) so we can slice telemetry precisely. Otherwise we must default to region-wide aggregates.
2) For retroactive emergency events older than 30 days we cannot guarantee full trace fidelity.
3) Regarding the 1.25x credit uplift: ops cannot commit to additional forensic runs beyond the stated evidence without executive sign-off — which Marissa already noted.

I'll prepare a short evidence template (attached) that lists the exact fields we will deliver and acceptable redaction. Happy to share a dummy CSV as an example.

Ben Carter
SRE, Redwood Inference
